axes.question: Quels critères explicites gouvernent la sélection avant traitement ?
Qui exerce concrètement le pouvoir de choisir/valider un sujet ?
Quels signaux externes alimentent la file de sujets ?
Existe-t-il une différence systématique documentée de sélection politique ?
Les financeurs ou plateformes commandent-ils les sujets sélectionnés ?
La sélection entraîne-t-elle automatiquement verdict, suppression ou effet politique ?

causal.gap: Need internal tasking records or quasi-experimental exposure/outcome evidence to close selection-control and political-effect links.
causal.limit: The chain is evidenced through candidate discovery and editorial selection, and partly through platform-linked downstream consequences; external command and political causal effect are not established.
causal.mechanism: universe of candidate claims -> monitoring/community/platform signals -> editorial selection criteria and judgement -> selected claim -> verification/verdict -> possible distribution/intervention consequences -> possible political effect

claims.claim: La sélection en amont est un pouvoir éditorial réel et documenté : les rédactions filtrent un univers de claims selon intérêt public, portée, dommage potentiel, actualité, vérifiabilité et ressources.
claims.gap: Les règles publiques ne capturent pas toutes les micro-décisions quotidiennes ni les sujets jamais considérés.

claims.claim: La décision de sélectionner et valider un sujet est principalement située dans la chaîne éditoriale interne documentée, non dans le verdict final lui-même.
claims.gap: Les documents publics ne révèlent pas toutes les discussions internes, consignes informelles ou arbitrages de conférence de rédaction.

claims.claim: Des signaux externes peuvent modifier la file de candidats : virality metrics, reader/community reports and platform-flagged material are explicitly used by multiple fact-checkers.
claims.gap: Candidate-pool influence does not establish external control over the final selection or verdict.

claims.claim: Une étude statistique publiée en 2025 trouve des différences systématiques entre six fact-checkers français compatibles avec un biais de sélection lié à l’orientation du média affilié.
claims.gap: L’étude identifie une association relative; elle ne connaît pas la distribution de vérité des déclarations candidates et ne ferme pas le mécanisme causal.

claims.claim: Le corpus n’établit pas qu’un propriétaire, financeur, État ou plateforme commande de manière générale quels sujets les fact-checkers doivent traiter.
claims.gap: Des contrats, instructions internes ou échanges non publics pourraient modifier cette conclusion s’ils documentaient un topic tasking spécifique.

claims.claim: Sélection du sujet, verdict, modération/suppression et effet politique sont des arêtes distinctes; aucune transition automatique entre elles n’est démontrée par ce corpus.
claims.gap: Les effets de sélection sur exposition, confiance, comportement ou résultat politique exigent des designs causaux séparés.

controls.control: Les standards IFCN/EFCSN exigent transparence de sélection et non-concentration indue sur un camp.
Plusieurs rédactions publient des critères de sélection explicites et non identiques, ce qui rend la sélection observable mais non aléatoire.
L’autorité éditoriale interne est explicitement documentée chez AFP, Reuters et par les exigences EFCSN.
Les plateformes et communautés peuvent alimenter la file de candidats sans que cela établisse à lui seul un commandement éditorial externe.
Des relations financières avec des plateformes existent et doivent être séparées de la preuve de tasking sur les sujets.
L’étude JEEA mesure des différences relatives de contenu mais ne dispose pas de la distribution vraie des fausses déclarations et ne prouve pas un contrôle causal par propriétaire, financeur ou État.

facts.subject: AFP selection: virality impact harm
facts.value: AFP states that its fact-checkers prioritize dubious online claims that are viral, impactful and potentially harmful to the public.

facts.subject: AFP selection: public interest and evidentiary feasibility
facts.value: AFP says it selects claims by assessing public interest and whether clear, sufficient evidence can be gathered; it does not publish a fact-check if strong cross-checked evidence cannot be established.

facts.subject: AFP selection: political neutrality rule
facts.value: AFP states it applies the same investigative approach regardless of claimant and does not focus on one candidate, party or website, while allowing more checks of consistent spreaders of potentially harmful misinformation.

facts.subject: AFP editorial authority over proposed checks
facts.value: AFP states that journalists liaise with regional editors, who discuss claims and proposed fact-checks, assess evidence needs and edit articles before publication.

facts.subject: AFP Meta candidate-pool input
facts.value: AFP states that posts flagged on Facebook and Instagram under Meta third-party fact checking are considered among the material it investigates.

facts.subject: IFCN selection standard
facts.value: IFCN requires signatories to consider reach and importance when selecting claims and to publish how they select claims.

facts.subject: IFCN methodology standard
facts.value: IFCN requires a public methodology covering selection, research, writing and publication, and says claims should be selected primarily on reach and importance.

facts.subject: IFCN state/political editorial-control boundary
facts.value: IFCN excludes organizations whose editorial work is controlled by a state, political party or politician, while allowing public-service funding when editorial control is clearly separated.

facts.subject: EFCSN impartiality selection constraint
facts.value: EFCSN requires verified members not to focus investigations unduly on one political party or side of the political spectrum.

facts.subject: EFCSN editorial-control transparency
facts.value: EFCSN requires members to make clear how and by whom editorial control is exercised and to identify editors or decision makers.

facts.subject: EFCSN funding and independence transparency
facts.value: EFCSN requires disclosure of platform/public income sources and an explanation of mechanisms ensuring editorial independence and the work funded by potentially conflicting sources.

facts.subject: Full Fact prioritizes prominence and reach
facts.value: Full Fact says a higher-profile claimant and wider reach can cause one claim to be selected over another.

facts.subject: Full Fact prioritizes repetition and harm
facts.value: Full Fact says repeated claims and claims with potential harm to people, institutions, groups or democratic processes receive greater priority.

facts.subject: Full Fact uses multiple secondary selection signals
facts.value: Full Fact lists Meta-partnership eligibility, virality, breaking-news relevance, novelty, reader requests and expected audience interest among additional considerations.

facts.subject: CORRECTIV selection criteria
facts.value: CORRECTIV says selection is necessary because not all online misinformation can be checked and lists current relevance, reach/virality and potential harm as key criteria.

facts.subject: CORRECTIV community input
facts.value: CORRECTIV says it searches proactively and also takes reader/community submissions through WhatsApp and its Faktenforum.

facts.subject: CORRECTIV Meta effect boundary
facts.value: CORRECTIV states its Meta-linked fact checks can trigger warnings and reduced reach, but that its fact-checking work does not control deletion decisions.

facts.subject: Maldita selection: virality
facts.value: Maldita says it prioritizes viral content using repeated reports, social diffusion, prominence of the sharer and circulation across formats.

facts.subject: Maldita selection: dangerousness
facts.value: Maldita says potentially harmful misinformation can be prioritized before it becomes viral, especially in health, emergencies, attacks, disasters or threats to social coexistence.

facts.subject: Maldita community shapes candidate discovery
facts.value: Maldita describes community reporting and collaborative platforms as inputs that help identify circulating misinformation and support investigations.

facts.subject: Reuters selection criteria
facts.value: Reuters Fact Check says material is selected using editorial value, potential real-world harm, actual reach, potential reach and separability of fact from opinion.

facts.subject: Reuters internal editorial control
facts.value: Reuters states its fact-check unit is within editorial and that its digital verification editor has editorial control of output with support from senior editors.

facts.subject: Reuters platform funding relationships
facts.value: Reuters discloses that Facebook and TikTok fund its fact-checking unit in exchange for content-authenticity or misinformation assessments, and that it provides fact-checking services to LinkedIn.

facts.subject: JEEA French fact-check dataset
facts.value: The 2025 JEEA study analyzes 2,405 articles from six main general-interest French fact-checkers through July 2021.

facts.subject: JEEA pooled alignment association
facts.value: In the study pooled specification, alignment between a fact-checker affiliated outlet and political orientation is associated with a 0.05 lower share of articles on that orientation, reported as statistically significant in the study.

facts.subject: JEEA selection asymmetry conclusion
facts.value: The study concludes that fact-checkers are relatively less likely to check ideologically aligned entities and, when they do, more likely to select statements they assess as correct.

facts.subject: JEEA causal and ground-truth limitation
facts.value: The study explicitly states that the underlying distribution of incorrect statements is unobserved, so the results cannot establish that all fact-checkers are biased from ground truth; content differences may also arise without deliberate rule violations.

facts.subject: Le Monde Décodeurs selection criteria
facts.value: Les Décodeurs state that claim selection depends on relevance to current events/public debate and factual verifiability; reader suggestions are further evaluated by source provenance, apparent veracity, virality and public importance.

run.scope: France/Europe 2019-2026; selection of claims/topics before verdict; compare transparent selection criteria, internal editorial authority, platform signals, and evidence of systematic selection differences; platform and international comparators only when mechanism-isomorphic.

ACTOR_NETWORK_MAP.relation: flagged material and paid assessment partnerships

COGNITIVE_MAP.query_guidance: separate public rules, observed content distributions, funding/interfaces and causal command; do not infer hidden tasking from correlation

speaker.goal: forensic assessment of upstream editorial selection
speaker.target: candidate universe -> selection -> treatment/verdict -> downstream effect

CONTRADICTION_LEDGER.contra: JEEA reports systematic cross-outlet political-content differences
CONTRADICTION_LEDGER.issue: declared nonpartisanship versus observed selection differences
CONTRADICTION_LEDGER.pro: IFCN/EFCSN and outlets state impartiality/non-concentration standards
CONTRADICTION_LEDGER.resolution: formal standards and empirical selection asymmetry can coexist; causal origin remains open

CONTRADICTION_LEDGER.contra: internal editorial control and independence requirements are also documented
CONTRADICTION_LEDGER.issue: platform/funder influence versus internal editorial control
CONTRADICTION_LEDGER.pro: platform funding and candidate signals are documented
CONTRADICTION_LEDGER.resolution: interface/resource influence is established; general topic command is not

DIALECTICAL_MAP.antithesis: Selection is explicitly filtered by reach, harm, relevance, verifiability and editorial judgment, and JEEA finds cross-outlet political-content differences.
DIALECTICAL_MAP.resolution: Published checks are not a random sample; selection effects are real, but the ground-truth candidate distribution is unobserved.
DIALECTICAL_MAP.thesis: Published fact checks are a neutral sample of political falsehoods.

DIALECTICAL_MAP.antithesis: Funding and platform candidate signals are documented, while standards and outlets describe internal editorial control and independence mechanisms.
DIALECTICAL_MAP.resolution: Resource/input relationships are real; topic-specific command requires a separate evidenced edge.
DIALECTICAL_MAP.thesis: Platform or public funding proves external editorial command.

DIALECTICAL_MAP.antithesis: Scarcity and published prioritization rules necessarily exclude many claims; no general deletion/control chain follows from omission.
DIALECTICAL_MAP.resolution: Omission may matter for agenda visibility but is not equivalent to suppression without additional action evidence.
DIALECTICAL_MAP.thesis: Not checking a claim is censorship or suppression.

corpus.circularity: LOW_TO_MODERATE; standards and member methods are related but not counted as independent proof of compliance
limits: JEEA ground truth candidate distribution unobserved

dimensions.temporal: 2019-2026 with 2021 Le Monde methodology version and 2021-ending dataset

IMPACT_MAP.agenda_visibility: VERIFIED_BOUNDED: selection determines which claims receive verification attention
IMPACT_MAP.platform_distribution: PARTIAL: some partnerships attach warnings/reduced reach; deletion not controlled by CORRECTIV fact checks

assumptions: published methodologies accurately describe formal policy but not every informal decision
JEEA coding/model are treated as study evidence with stated limitations
absence of public tasking records is not proof none exist
implicit: selection criteria shape observed agenda before verdict
external signals may affect candidate discovery without command
MANIPULATION_REPORT.query_guidance: prefer current first-party methodologies; use peer-reviewed study for observed content differences; preserve causal limits

rhetorical.AUTH: method pages establish declared rules and roles, not perfect compliance
rhetorical.DEM: selection differences do not by themselves prove suppression
rhetorical.FAC: separate candidate discovery, selection, verdict, moderation and effect
rhetorical.NUM: JEEA coefficient is association within its design, not universal bias rate

negative_results: no evidence that omission alone equals suppression
not_computable: counterfactual universe of all equally checkable claims
MODULE_EXECUTION.reason: topic selection determines which claims enter the verification frame before verdict

negative_results: general owner/funder/platform topic tasking not established
operations_applied: tested funding/platform inputs against topic-command inference
MODULE_EXECUTION.reason: selection requires authority over agenda and proposed checks

NEXT_QUERIES: RECHECK if internal editorial calendars, rejected-candidate logs or assignment messages become accessible
RECHECK if platform contracts specify claim/topic quotas or mandatory tasking
RECHECK JEEA result if a later replication with observable candidate denominators appears
DEFER political-effect claim pending exposure/outcome design

RESOURCE_FLOW_MAP.boundary: funding/service relation documented; topic tasking not established
candidate-pool input documented; final selection command not established

RESPONSIBILITY_MAP.boundary: role, funding, affiliation or correlation do not establish topic-specific command or intent
not_established: general owner command over selected topics
general platform command over final topic selection
intentional partisan manipulation by individual editors
verified: fact-check teams exercise selection under published criteria
editors exercise internal review/control in documented cases
platforms may supply signals/funding and apply downstream distribution mechanisms

evidence_limits: public methodologies omit some internal deliberations
